author: christina_rossetti
text:
There is no place that I would rather be
Than here beside you, my dearest one;
No place to wander where our faces see,
Nor shall there come from your eyes such tears as mine!

O sweet face turned away and lost again
In those dark pools of thine own soul's love;
But yet how fair thy pale forehead shines!
With all its lines of thought, its very brow.

My heart goes out beyond this little space:
Oh, not within these walls with you can live
I cannot tell what I could do or say,

author: edna_millay
text:
It's late, I see that you are up,
Let me try to write you one;
And as it is my first attempt
I do not know if this will be fit.

Perhaps there may be too much thought
In such an artificial thing;
But I think when two or three meet
To talk on common things, we cling
With what we can best say and sing.

text: The poet’s perspective is that God has always been there for us despite our wrongdoings. We should never lose hope because His mercy endures forever. The reader could be encouraged by knowing they are cared about even when doing evil.

author: christina_rossetti
text:
My face is turned from you, I turn not back:
I would not hear your voice again; no more,
No more, my love, I'll listen to thy song.

For wherefore should I seek for that which cannot come?
O tell me why must it be so hard to part?
But we have parted now, and therefore know
What parting means--what it brings after it,
And what it takes away. What is left of us
But tears, and bitter words unsaid, and sorrow?

Haiku, as an ancient Japanese poetic form, has evolved over centuries into a concise expression of nature and human emotions. The format consists of three lines: the first with five syllables, the second with seven syllables, and the third with five again. Haikus often convey a profound sense of time and space through vivid imagery that captures the essence of fleeting moments or universal truths. Through their minimalist yet evocative language, haiku poets invite readers to experience the beauty and complexity of life's most fundamental aspects.

author: edna_millay
text:
When I am dead, my dearest,

Sing no sad songs for me;
Plant thou no roses at my head,
Nor shady cypress tree:

Be the green grass above me
With showers and dewdrops wet;
And if thou wilt, remember,
And If thou wilt not, forget.

I shall not see the shadows,
I shall only be;
The light that shines from heaven
A breath more bright than ever.

author: edwin_arlington_robinson
text:
When Love Is Come

Love, come!
And let there be
A heart so deep and sweet
That all the world may see
The treasure that I keep:
An hour of love between us two
Between me and you
To-day, tomorrow, always
Will I hold this place to you

text: It has been raining all day long, so there are puddles everywhere outside my house. My mother says these puddles might get deep enough to fill up my shoes. How could this happen? It would be great if we were able to understand our mothers better!

How do you make a person whole? We need to look into their eyes. To see beyond that facade and find them… the heart-shaped piece missing from within. author: edna_millay
text: In this poem you write an account of life without love; it might be something like "winter" or some other metaphor related to love (in fact we may find several such metaphors later). But then there is a change at the end of the third stanza, where we realize that this isn't really about winter but rather about loving somebody who has no interest in our feelings. The speaker feels rejected yet continues caring for his beloved one even though she doesn't respond in kind.

author: edwin_arlington_robinson
text:
With all your might, and with your tears I cry;
You are so beautiful, my darling, how you shine!
What a clear light shines from your hair--and why?
I see you smile as you sit by me to-night.
I want you always: yet what is this?
To tell it straight out seems wrong, but when?

author: emily_dickinson
text:
I would like to see my sister and brother again,
But I'm so far away from home.
They have gone out into the world with me,
And they are on their way home.

It is hard for you to be alone in this place,
To hear your mother call you by name;
But you must not forget that God knows all things.

Faro, I want to write you a little something just to tell you what we are doing. Our new home is far from the sea and does not have an ocean view like your house in California. But don't worry - as soon as winter arrives, my family will be back in our old house by the seaside. We will live there for at least one more year. Then perhaps we can move here permanently if everything goes well. author: edwin_arlington_robinson
text:
I saw your name on his shoulder-blade, written
in blood. I think it is my fault that you died,
the blood on his face like ink, which flowed from
his head while still alive. And how do we know?
We see him dead lying on the road near our town,
but then again, maybe some time ago this was me,
and the man next to me now with arms wrapped
around me when I cried out ‘Stop! Please stop!’

author: edwin_arlington_robinson
text:
All things are dear to me, and some more dear;
And I must lead my life, though every step is doubt.

One day one way that seemed the quickest may
Have led me through a field of blinding mist.

The sun was low and it seemed an evening walk,
But other feet were walking too quickly on my track.

When I reached where they had paused I found them gone.
I turned away and groped about for stones,
To keep my balance on the slippery ground.

Hiligaynon is a language spoken by more than 10 million people, mostly living within an area known as Western Visayas. This region includes Panay Island and some neighboring islands such as Negros, Guimaras, Masbate, Romblon, etc. It is one of seven Philippine languages officially recognized for being used on road signs (in addition to Tagalog and English). Hiligaynon also has official status at two local government units - Silay City and San Carlos City.

At first my mind was blank
I didn’t know where to start
But then I thought about my life with her
This girl I used to call my wife
Now it is past tense but still very real
She made me feel like I mattered
When I felt like nobody cared
And now that I am apart from her
My heart feels like it is breaking
Oh how do we make things right
How can I get through this day

Not even if we’re together
All because you are gone away

author: emily_dickinson
text:
The little children, all so bright and gay,
Have come to watch the circus go away;
A little while they saw it pass along,
And then, when all was done, they went home again.
How much is left of us, that's true, but we must be thankful for what is left,--
All our old friends who will not let us forget them,
But keep on coming back like this sweet little band
To see us grow up older every year--they can't understand.

author: john_masefield
text:
O sun, what need hast thou to shine so bright?
In such a world as this, there is no light.

The sun that shines on us so cold and hard,
It has no heart nor sense or mind; it's just an orb:
And when he goes from us at night, he carries his heart with him,
For we do not understand, and see our joy depart!

Then God has made for me another sun:
He lives within my heart, whose rays are warm;
With those I meet today shall be one whole day,

author: john_masefield
text:
We are the flowers that bloom and die,
The sunbeams that fade to darkness;
The birds who sing songs by night:
And we shall be gone when morning comes.

But what have you left for us?
Nothing but words upon your pages;
Only memories of your smiles,
Your deeds, your faces and your laughter--

O all I know is this:
That life's so very fleeting,
As time keeps passing on...

author: matthew_arnold
text:
Ah, well! What is there to do?
That I should mourn my first love's doom?
Who can escape, or turn from her,
The hand that holds him fast in hell?

And yet,--but here let me change tone;
My heart has left his side at last,
And I have loved another one:
Is he not worth this sacrifice?

The mind begins to see an infinite dream
Of worlds and forms of life beside us unseen:

author: matthew_arnold
text:
I know not what to write about,
The love I have for thee and naught;
But still my soul shall be thine own,
And with its life will give itself away
To all thy future days: so let me die!

How much it grieves me now that thou
Canst never love again as yet,—
That love which is too deep for earth
To touch till death doth part the twain.

text:
When you can remember that,
Your sadness has grown so deep.
You never stop crying about it,
I feel as if it is happening right now.

The last words on your lips are so true,
Because what they said was right on the mark.
But when we were still young,
We used to dance together,
With our hearts full of love for one another.

author: matthew_arnold
text:
And yet, when all is said and done,
The day will be fair at last;
With silver skies and stars that shine,
There will come back to me again
My darling, lovely lost one!

For this world's sunshine bright as gold,
Is but its darkling side's eclipse;
Yet brighter shines the sunlit fold
Than the black night that has gone by:
I know my own sweet love shall hold
That I have sung of so fondly.

author: stephen_crane
text:
A few nights ago my heart was heavy,
For what can be greater than a bounteous heart?
I gazed into an empty bowl before me,
In my mind's eye, I saw nothing but despair.

"Oh how beautiful!" a voice cried out;
Like a shooting star across my sky.
The light from which shone so brightly,
Like those who gaze upon us all day long.

author: stephen_crane
text:
The Night-Comer

The night-comer, the night-comber,
the night-walker, the midnight-cramer;
He who walks in his sleep, he who lies awake all night
With arms akimbo and eyes distended wide--
Who are you? What have you done or seen to make your
body so tense? Who are you that do not rest, but stalk
through the streets? What is it you seek here at this hour?
You must come back to bed again: it is time for sleep.

author: christina_rossetti
text:
And then there came a voice from out the night,
That made me wish I had been born again;
The very word that fell on my ear was sweet
As honey to an ant: "Behold! thy son is dead!"

I knew no more than if it were but light
To hear again such news as he would tell.
"Oh, mother, mother," cried I, as he ran by,
"Ah me, ah me, I'm weary and old and ill."
